class CausalGenerator(GeneratorMixin):
    """Base class for causal defect generators.

    Parameters
    ----------
    random_generator : numpy.random.Generator, default=rng(seed=0)
        Random number generator instance.
    dgp : DGP or None, default=None
        DGP instance (fitted or unfitted). This is the ONLY structure
        the generator accepts — a DGP carries its own graph and
        column_mapping. There is no graph-only configuration and no
        implicit default backend: if ``dgp`` is None, ``generate()``
        raises (build one with e.g.
        ``GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping))``).

    Notes
    -----
    No generator-side ``fit``, no graph-only configuration
        Causal generators have NO public ``fit()`` — the only fitted
        object is the DGP (``DGP.fit``), consistent with the rest of the
        library. The DGP is fitted either EXPLICITLY by the caller
        (preferred) or lazily INSIDE ``generate()`` when the configured
        DGP is still unfitted (``_require_dgp``).

    Pipelines
        In a pipeline, each causal stage receives the PREVIOUS stage's
        output as input. Fitting the DGP lazily on that contaminated
        input would refit the world per stage (and, with NaN-bearing
        columns, trigger complete-case filtering). Fit the DGP ONCE on
        the clean entry data and share the fitted instance::

            dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)  # fit on clean X

            missingness = CausalMissingnessGenerator(rng=..., dgp=dgp)
            Xm, _ = missingness.generate(X, None, ...)

            drift = CausalDriftGenerator(rng=..., dgp=dgp)  # share
            Xt, _ = drift.generate(Xm, None, ...)

        All per-stage scale computations are NaN-safe, so even the lazy
        refit path behaves sensibly; the explicitly-fitted shared
        ``dgp=`` pattern simply guarantees ONE world for the whole
        pipeline. Fit the DGP once on clean data — the backends do not
        impute or filter NaN rows at fit time.
    """

    #: Subclasses set this to the deficit name used in labels.
    deficit_name = "causal"

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0), dgp=None):
        self.random_generator = random_generator
        self.dgp = dgp
        self.graph = None if dgp is None else dgp.graph
        self.column_mapping = None if dgp is None else dgp.column_mapping
        # Per-row deficit labels of the last generated output. Subclasses
        # fill this in ``generate()`` and expose it through their own
        # public getter (e.g. ``get_outliers_labels()``) which raises
        # RuntimeError when no output has been generated yet.
        self.deficit_labels_ = None

    # -- DGP plumbing -------------------------------------------------------

    def use_dgp(self, dgp):
        """Attach a DGP (fitted or unfitted); the structure comes with it.

        An unfitted DGP is fitted lazily inside ``generate()`` on the
        generate-time data (``_require_dgp``). Prefer attaching a DGP you
        fitted explicitly on the clean entry data (shared across a
        pipeline).
        """
        self.dgp = dgp
        self.graph = dgp.graph
        self.column_mapping = dgp.column_mapping

    def _require_fitted(self):
        if self.graph is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Generator has no structure: pass a dgp=... to the "
                "constructor, or use use_dgp(dgp), before generate()."
            )

    def _require_dgp(self, X=None):
        """Require a fitted DGP; fit lazily on demand.

        Call ``_require_dgp(X)`` before any column mutation so the DGP is
        fitted on the ORIGINAL data. Two routes:

        1. a fitted DGP was configured/attached — nothing to do;
        2. an UNFITTED DGP was configured/attached — it is fitted here
           on ``X`` (the generate-time data).

        There is NO implicit default backend: if no DGP was given,
        ``generate()`` fails. Build the world explicitly, e.g.
        ``dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm(graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)``.
        """
        if self.dgp is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "This generator needs a DGP: pass a dgp=... to the "
                "constructor, or use use_dgp(dgp), before generate(). "
                "Build one with e.g. dgp = GcmSCMDGP(make_gcm_scm("
                "graph, column_mapping)).fit(X)."
            )
        elif not self.dgp.is_fitted():
            self.dgp.fit(X)

    def _sample(self, n_samples):
        """Delegate sampling to the fitted DGP."""
        if self.dgp is None or not self.dgp.is_fitted():
            raise RuntimeError(
                "_sample requires a fitted DGP: pass a fitted dgp=... to "
                "the constructor (or use_dgp(dgp)) first."
            )
        return self.dgp.sample(self.random_generator, n_samples)

    # -- Mechanism gating (Distinction 3) -----------------------------------

    def _fire_masks(self, rows, perturbation_nodes, selector=None):
        """Fire masks for ALL rows at once: dict {node: bool row-mask}.

        Delegates to a ``Selector`` from ``badgers.core.selectors``:
        ``selector(rows, y) -> {node: bool mask}``.
        ``None`` defaults to ``AlwaysSelector`` (every row fires).

        Parameters
        ----------
        rows : array to gate (the generator's working rows -- for the noise
            generator these are the n_copies-EXPANDED rows).
        perturbation_nodes : list of str, non-empty (pre-validated).
        selector : Selector or None, default None
            The row-selection rule. ``None`` = ``AlwaysSelector`` (all
            rows fire). Presets: ``BernoulliSelector`` (iid rate),
            ``ExactCountSelector`` (exact count), ``TopQuantileSelector``
            (value threshold, self or driver mode), ``AlwaysSelector``;
            any user callable with the same signature works.

        Note: masks are computed against ``rows`` BEFORE any mutation
        (callers write NaNs/noise afterwards), which makes the gate
        order-independent -- the "compute ALL masks first" invariant the
        legacy missingness path already documented.
        """
        if selector is None:
            return {
                node: np.ones(rows.shape[0], dtype=bool)
                for node in perturbation_nodes
            }
        return selector(rows, None)

    # -- Validation ---------------------------------------------------------

    def _validate_structure(self, X):
        """Validate the configured structure against the input data.

        Raises ``ValueError`` when:

        - no DGP is configured (no graph / column_mapping available);
        - the graph is not a valid DAG;
        - ``X`` has as many columns as the graph has nodes;
        - the column_mapping is a dict covering exactly the graph nodes
          with unique, in-range integer column indices.

        Returns nothing: all state needed downstream lives on ``self``
        (``self.graph``, ``self.column_mapping``).
        """
        graph = self.graph
        column_mapping = self.column_mapping
        if graph is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "no DGP configured: pass a dgp=... to the constructor, "
                "or use use_dgp(dgp) (the DGP carries graph and "
                "column_mapping)"
            )
        validate_dag(graph)
        n_features = X.shape[1]
        if n_features != len(graph.nodes):
            raise ValueError(
                f"X has {n_features} columns but graph has "
                f"{len(graph.nodes)} nodes"
            )
        if column_mapping is None:
            raise ValueError("column_mapping parameter is required")
        if not isinstance(column_mapping, dict):
            raise ValueError(
                "column_mapping must be a dict, "
                f"got {type(column_mapping).__name__}"
            )
        for node in graph.nodes:
            if not isinstance(node, str):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"graph nodes must be strings, "
                    f"got {type(node).__name__} for node '{node}'"
                )
        missing = set(graph.nodes) - set(column_mapping.keys())
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"column_mapping missing node(s): {sorted(missing)}"
            )
        extra = set(column_mapping.keys()) - set(graph.nodes)
        if extra:
            raise ValueError(
                f"column_mapping has unknown node(s): {sorted(extra)}"
            )
        seen = {}
        for node, idx in column_mapping.items():
            if not isinstance(idx, int):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column_mapping values must be int, "
                    f"got {type(idx).__name__} for node '{node}'"
                )
            if idx < 0 or idx >= n_features:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"column index {idx} for node '{node}' "
                    f"is out of range [0, {n_features - 1}]"
                )
            if idx in seen:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"duplicate column index {idx} "
                    f"for nodes {sorted([seen[idx], node])}"
                )
            seen[idx] = node

    def _validate_perturbation_nodes(self, perturbation_nodes):
        """Validate the perturbation nodes against the configured graph.

        Requires a non-empty list of nodes that exist in the graph.
        Raises ``ValueError`` otherwise; returns nothing.
        """
        graph = self.graph
        if graph is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "no DGP configured: pass a dgp=... to the constructor, "
                "or use use_dgp(dgp) (the DGP carries graph and "
                "column_mapping)"
            )
        if perturbation_nodes is None:
            raise ValueError("perturbation_nodes parameter is required")
        if not isinstance(perturbation_nodes, list):
            raise ValueError(
                "perturbation_nodes must be a list, "
                f"got {type(perturbation_nodes).__name__}"
            )
        if len(perturbation_nodes) == 0:
            raise ValueError("perturbation_nodes must not be empty")
        for node in perturbation_nodes:
            if node not in graph.nodes:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"perturbation node '{node}' not found in graph"
                )

class FixedShiftClassesGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    """
    Deterministically shift the rows fired by a selector, independently per
    class — the non-random counterpart of :class:`RandomShiftClassesGenerator`.

    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1); each class value of the
    class column gets an exact shift (no draw), applied to the rows fired by
    the selector. The class data lives in a column of ``X`` (``y`` is not
    used for selection). Repeated calls with the same input return the same
    output.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize the FixedShiftClassesGenerator (no random generator needed)."""
        super().__init__(random_generator=None)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, *, selector=None, shift=0.1, variables=None, class_column=None):
        """
        Deterministically shift the rows fired by the selector, one exact
        shift per class value of the class column.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through unchanged; not used for selection).
        :param selector: A selector deciding which rows are shifted (required; its masks
                         are OR-ed to the affected rows).
        :param shift: The exact shift applied to the fired rows of each class, in units of
                      column standard deviation (data are standardized first). A single
                      float (same shift for every class and column), a vector (one entry
                      per shifted column, same for every class), or a dict
                      ``{class_value: float or vector}`` — fired rows whose class value
                      is absent from the dict are not shifted.
        :param variables: Columns to shift. Either a list of column positions (ints) or a
                          list of variable names resolvable through
                          ``selector.column_mapping``. Defaults to all columns except the
                          class column.
        :param class_column: The column holding the class values: either its position
                             (int) or a variable name resolvable through
                             ``selector.column_mapping``. The class column groups the
                             fired rows (one shift per class value) and is never shifted
                             itself. If omitted, it is recovered from the selector's
                             ``column_mapping``; when neither is available, all fired
                             rows are treated as one class and every column may be
                             shifted.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        if selector is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "FixedShiftClassesGenerator needs a selector deciding "
                "which rows shift (e.g. ClassSelector over the class "
                "column): classes are columns of X, y is not used for "
                "selection."
            )
        masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
        fired = masks[0] if len(masks) == 1 else np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
        if not fired.any():
            return X, y
        # resolve the class column: explicit parameter first, selector sniffing as fallback
        class_col = class_column
        if class_col is not None and isinstance(class_col, str):
            mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
            pos = mapping.get(class_col) if mapping is not None else None
            if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve class column {class_col!r} in X")
            class_col = pos
        elif class_col is None:
            class_col = resolve_class_column(selector, X)
        elif not (0 <= class_col < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(f"class_column {class_col} is not a valid column position in X")
        shifts = shift if isinstance(shift, dict) else None
        if shifts is not None and class_col is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "a dict shift requires a class column: pass "
                "class_column (int or name) or use a selector with "
                "column_mapping to resolve the class column position"
            )
        # resolve which columns are shifted
        if variables is not None:
            mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
            cols = []
            for var in variables:
                pos = mapping.get(var) if mapping is not None and isinstance(var, str) else var
                if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                    raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve shift column {var!r} in X")
                cols.append(pos)
            cols = np.array(sorted(set(cols)), dtype=int)
        else:
            # all columns except the class column
            cols = np.array([i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if i != class_col], dtype=int)
        if cols.size == 0:
            return X, y
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # one exact shift per class value among the fired rows
        if class_col is not None:
            values = np.unique(X[fired, class_col])
        else:
            values = np.array([None])
        for value in values:
            if shifts is not None:
                if value not in shifts:
                    continue
                shift_value = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(shifts[value], dtype=float), (cols.size,))
            elif isinstance(shift, np.ndarray) and shift.ndim == 1:
                shift_value = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(shift, dtype=float), (cols.size,))
            else:
                shift_value = np.full(cols.size, float(shift))
            rows = fired if class_col is None else (fired & (X[:, class_col] == value))
            Xt[np.ix_(rows, cols)] += shift_value
        # inverse transform
        return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

class FixedShiftGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    r"""
    Deterministically shift (geometrical translation) values of each column
    independently of one another — the non-random counterpart of
    :class:`RandomShiftGenerator`.

    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1), then each column is
    translated by exactly ``shift_std``: the ith column becomes
    `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \text{shift\_std}_i$`. No random number is drawn,
    so repeated calls with the same input return the same output.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize the FixedShiftGenerator (no random generator needed)."""
        super().__init__(random_generator=None)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, shift_std: Union[float, np.array, list] = 0.1):
        r"""
        Deterministically shift each column by exactly ``shift_std``.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through unchanged; not used in this implementation).
        :param shift_std: Shift applied to each column. A single float (applied to all columns)
                          or an array of floats (one per column). The value is the shift in
                          units of column standard deviation (data are standardized first):
                          a positive entry moves the column up, a negative entry moves it
                          down. The same input always produces the same output.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        shift_std = np.asarray(shift_std, dtype=float)
        if shift_std.ndim == 1 and shift_std.size > 1:
            assert shift_std.size == X.shape[
                1], f"shift_std length ({shift_std.size}) must equal number of features in X ({X.shape[1]})"
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # exact shift per column: |shift_std| magnitude, sign(shift_std) direction
        shift = np.broadcast_to(shift_std, (X.shape[1],))
        # add shift
        Xt += shift
        # inverse transform
        return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

class RandomShiftClassesGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    """
    Randomly shift (geometrical translation) the rows fired by a selector,
    independently per class.

    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1); for each class value
    of the class column a random shift is drawn and added to the FIRED rows
    of that class. The class data lives in a column of ``X`` (``y`` is not
    used for selection).
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        Initialize the RandomShiftClassesGenerator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, *, selector=None, shift_std=0.1, variables=None, class_column=None):
        """
        Randomly shift the rows fired by the selector, one independent
        shift per class value of the class column.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through unchanged; not used for selection).
        :param selector: A selector deciding which rows are shifted. A
                         :class:`badgers.core.selectors.ClassSelector` over
                         the class column (typical), or any selector whose
                         masks OR to the fired rows. The per-class lookup
                         requires ``selector.column_mapping`` to resolve the
                         class column position. Required (a per-class rule
                         has no class-free default).
        :param shift_std: Standard deviation of the normal distribution from
                          which the shifts are drawn. Entries are SIGNED: the
                          magnitude (``abs``) is the scale of the draw and the
                          sign is the shift direction — a negative entry drifts
                          the class downward. A single float (same magnitude for
                          every class, one independent draw per class) or a dict
                          ``{class_value: float}``. Fired rows whose class value
                          is absent from the dict are not shifted.
        :param variables: Columns to shift. Either a list of column positions
                          (ints) or a list of variable names resolvable through
                          ``selector.column_mapping``. Defaults to all columns
                          except the class column — the class column is
                          identification metadata and is never shifted by
                          default (shifting it would move rows away from
                          their class values).
        :param class_column: The column holding the class values: either its
                          position (int) or a variable name resolvable through
                          ``selector.column_mapping``. The class column groups
                          the fired rows (one shift per class value) and is
                          never shifted itself. If omitted, it is recovered
                          from the selector's ``column_mapping``; when neither
                          is available, all fired rows are treated as one
                          class and every column may be shifted.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        if selector is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "RandomShiftClassesGenerator needs a selector deciding "
                "which rows shift (e.g. ClassSelector over the class "
                "column): classes are columns of X, y is not used for "
                "selection."
            )
        masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
        fired = masks[0] if len(masks) == 1 else np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
        if not fired.any():
            return X, y
        # resolve the class column: explicit parameter first, selector sniffing as fallback
        class_col = class_column
        if class_col is not None and isinstance(class_col, str):
            mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
            pos = mapping.get(class_col) if mapping is not None else None
            if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve class column {class_col!r} in X")
            class_col = pos
        elif class_col is None:
            class_col = resolve_class_column(selector, X)
        elif not (0 <= class_col < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(f"class_column {class_col} is not a valid column position in X")
        stds = shift_std if isinstance(shift_std, dict) else None
        if stds is not None and class_col is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "a dict shift_std requires a class column: pass "
                "class_column (int or name) or use a selector with "
                "column_mapping to resolve the class column position"
            )
        # resolve which columns are shifted
        if variables is not None:
            mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
            cols = []
            for var in variables:
                pos = mapping.get(var) if mapping is not None and isinstance(var, str) else var
                if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                    raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve shift column {var!r} in X")
                cols.append(pos)
            cols = np.array(sorted(set(cols)), dtype=int)
        else:
            # all columns except the class column
            cols = np.array([i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if i != class_col], dtype=int)
        if cols.size == 0:
            return X, y
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # one independent shift per class value among the fired rows
        if class_col is not None:
            values = np.unique(X[fired, class_col])
        else:
            values = np.array([None])
        for value in values:
            if stds is not None:
                if value not in stds:
                    continue
                std = stds[value]
            else:
                std = shift_std
            rows = fired if class_col is None else (fired & (X[:, class_col] == value))
            # signed magnitude: |std| is the scale, sign(std) the direction
            shift = self.random_generator.normal(loc=0, scale=abs(std), size=cols.size)
            Xt[np.ix_(rows, cols)] += np.sign(std) * shift
        # inverse transform
        return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

                     masks OR to the fired rows. The per-class lookup
                     requires ``selector.column_mapping`` to resolve the
                     class column position. Required (a per-class rule
                     has no class-free default).
    :param shift_std: Standard deviation of the normal distribution from
                      which the shifts are drawn. Entries are SIGNED: the
                      magnitude (``abs``) is the scale of the draw and the
                      sign is the shift direction — a negative entry drifts
                      the class downward. A single float (same magnitude for
                      every class, one independent draw per class) or a dict
                      ``{class_value: float}``. Fired rows whose class value
                      is absent from the dict are not shifted.
    :param variables: Columns to shift. Either a list of column positions
                      (ints) or a list of variable names resolvable through
                      ``selector.column_mapping``. Defaults to all columns
                      except the class column — the class column is
                      identification metadata and is never shifted by
                      default (shifting it would move rows away from
                      their class values).
    :param class_column: The column holding the class values: either its
                      position (int) or a variable name resolvable through
                      ``selector.column_mapping``. The class column groups
                      the fired rows (one shift per class value) and is
                      never shifted itself. If omitted, it is recovered
                      from the selector's ``column_mapping``; when neither
                      is available, all fired rows are treated as one
                      class and every column may be shifted.
    :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
    """
    if selector is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "RandomShiftClassesGenerator needs a selector deciding "
            "which rows shift (e.g. ClassSelector over the class "
            "column): classes are columns of X, y is not used for "
            "selection."
        )
    masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
    fired = masks[0] if len(masks) == 1 else np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
    if not fired.any():
        return X, y
    # resolve the class column: explicit parameter first, selector sniffing as fallback
    class_col = class_column
    if class_col is not None and isinstance(class_col, str):
        mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
        pos = mapping.get(class_col) if mapping is not None else None
        if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve class column {class_col!r} in X")
        class_col = pos
    elif class_col is None:
        class_col = resolve_class_column(selector, X)
    elif not (0 <= class_col < X.shape[1]):
        raise ValueError(f"class_column {class_col} is not a valid column position in X")
    stds = shift_std if isinstance(shift_std, dict) else None
    if stds is not None and class_col is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "a dict shift_std requires a class column: pass "
            "class_column (int or name) or use a selector with "
            "column_mapping to resolve the class column position"
        )
    # resolve which columns are shifted
    if variables is not None:
        mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
        cols = []
        for var in variables:
            pos = mapping.get(var) if mapping is not None and isinstance(var, str) else var
            if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve shift column {var!r} in X")
            cols.append(pos)
        cols = np.array(sorted(set(cols)), dtype=int)
    else:
        # all columns except the class column
        cols = np.array([i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if i != class_col], dtype=int)
    if cols.size == 0:
        return X, y
    # normalize X
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    scaler.fit(X)
    Xt = scaler.transform(X)
    # one independent shift per class value among the fired rows
    if class_col is not None:
        values = np.unique(X[fired, class_col])
    else:
        values = np.array([None])
    for value in values:
        if stds is not None:
            if value not in stds:
                continue
            std = stds[value]
        else:
            std = shift_std
        rows = fired if class_col is None else (fired & (X[:, class_col] == value))
        # signed magnitude: |std| is the scale, sign(std) the direction
        shift = self.random_generator.normal(loc=0, scale=abs(std), size=cols.size)
        Xt[np.ix_(rows, cols)] += np.sign(std) * shift
    # inverse transform
    return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

class RandomShiftGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    r"""
    Randomly shift (geometrical translation) values of each column independently of one another.
    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1) and a random number is added to each column.
    The ith columns is simply translated: `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \epsilon_i$`
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        Initialize the RandomShiftGenerator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, shift_std: Union[float, np.array, list] = 0.1):
        r"""
        Randomly shift (geometrical translation) values of each column independently of one another.
        Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1), and a random number drawn from a normal distribution
        with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. `shift_std` is then added to each column.
        The ith column is simply translated: `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \epsilon_i$`, where $\epsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \text{shift\_std})$.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable, a 1D array-like object (optional). Not used in this implementation.
        :param shift_std: Magnitude of the random shift applied to each column. Can be a single float
                          (applied to all columns) or an array of floats (one per column). The values
                          are interpreted as standard deviations: a random number drawn from a normal
                          distribution is multiplied by ``shift_std`` (absolute value used as the
                          scale, the sign used as the shift direction). A negative entry shifts the
                          column in the negative direction.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        # check that if shift_std is an array, it is of length == X.shape[1]
        shift_std = np.asarray(shift_std, dtype=float)
        if shift_std.ndim == 1 and shift_std.size > 1:
            assert shift_std.size == X.shape[
                1], f"shift_std length ({shift_std.size}) must equal number of features in X ({X.shape[1]})"
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # generate random values for the shift for each column
        # scale must be non-negative: use |shift_std| as the scale and sign(shift_std) as the direction
        scale = np.broadcast_to(np.abs(shift_std), (X.shape[1],))
        sign = np.broadcast_to(np.sign(shift_std), (X.shape[1],))
        shift = self.random_generator.normal(loc=0, scale=scale, size=X.shape[1]) * sign
        # add shift
        Xt += shift
        # inverse transform
        return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

class CausalDriftGenerator(CausalGenerator):
    """Generates causally-propagated systematic drift.

    Parameters
    ----------
    random_generator : numpy.random.Generator, default=rng(seed=0)
        Random number generator instance.
    dgp : DGP or None, default=None
        DGP instance (passed via the constructor or use_dgp(); fitted
        explicitly by the caller, or lazily inside generate() if
        unfitted).

    generate() parameters (passed via **params)
    ----------
    perturbation_nodes : list of str
        Nodes where the drift is injected (required).
    selector : Selector or None, default=None
        Row-selection rule from ``badgers.core.selectors``
        (``AlwaysSelector``, ``BernoulliSelector``, ``ExactCountSelector``,
        ``TopQuantileSelector``, or any callable with the same signature).
        ``None`` = every row fires.
    drift_std : float or np.ndarray, default=0.5
        Std of the systematic shift, relative to column std. Scalar or
        per-perturbation-node.
    """

    deficit_name = "drift"

    def get_drift_labels(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return the drift labels of the last generated output.

        A boolean vector aligned with the rows of the last generated
        output: True for rows that carry the drift deficit, False for
        original rows.
        """
        if self.deficit_labels_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Drift labels are only available after calling generate()."
            )
        return self.deficit_labels_

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(
        self,
        X,
        y,
        perturbation_nodes=None,
        selector=None,
        drift_std=0.5,
    ):
        """Inject causally-propagated systematic drift in place."""
        self._require_fitted()
        self._require_dgp(X)
        self._validate_structure(X)
        self._validate_perturbation_nodes(perturbation_nodes)
        node_to_col = self.column_mapping
        n_samples = X.shape[0]
        col_stds = _column_stds(X)

        if np.isscalar(drift_std):
            drift_scale = np.full(len(perturbation_nodes), float(drift_std))
        else:
            drift_scale = np.asarray(drift_std, dtype=float)
            if drift_scale.shape != (len(perturbation_nodes),):
                raise ValueError(
                    "drift_std array must have one entry per perturbation node"
                )

        # Draw the systematic shift ONCE (applied to all rows).
        shifts = {}
        for j, node in enumerate(perturbation_nodes):
            col = node_to_col[node]
            shifts[col] = self.random_generator.normal(
                0, drift_scale[j] * col_stds[col]
            )

        # Apply the shift to the perturbation nodes (gated by the selector:
        # fire masks for ALL rows at once, thresholds on the un-mutated data).
        fires = self._fire_masks(
            X, perturbation_nodes, selector=selector,
        )
        affected = np.zeros(n_samples, dtype=bool)
        for node in perturbation_nodes:
            mask = fires[node]
            col = node_to_col[node]
            X[mask, col] += shifts[col]
            affected |= mask

        # Recompute the descendants of the AFFECTED rows through the
        # structural equations (Pearl surgery): descendant = f(new parents)
        # + fresh noise. The shift at the perturbation node is systematic
        # (a single shift applied to all affected rows); unaffected rows
        # are left untouched.
        affected_rows = np.flatnonzero(affected)
        if affected_rows.size:
            sub = X[affected_rows]
            self.dgp.intervene(
                sub, perturbation_nodes, rng=self.random_generator
            )
            X[affected_rows] = sub

        self.deficit_labels_ = affected.copy()
        return X, None

class FixedShiftClassesGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    """
    Deterministically shift the rows fired by a selector, independently per
    class — the non-random counterpart of :class:`RandomShiftClassesGenerator`.

    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1); each class value of the
    class column gets an exact shift (no draw), applied to the rows fired by
    the selector. The class data lives in a column of ``X`` (``y`` is not
    used for selection). Repeated calls with the same input return the same
    output.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize the FixedShiftClassesGenerator (no random generator needed)."""
        super().__init__(random_generator=None)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, *, selector=None, shift=0.1, variables=None, class_column=None):
        """
        Deterministically shift the rows fired by the selector, one exact
        shift per class value of the class column.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through unchanged; not used for selection).
        :param selector: A selector deciding which rows are shifted (required; its masks
                         are OR-ed to the affected rows).
        :param shift: The exact shift applied to the fired rows of each class, in units of
                      column standard deviation (data are standardized first). A single
                      float (same shift for every class and column), a vector (one entry
                      per shifted column, same for every class), or a dict
                      ``{class_value: float or vector}`` — fired rows whose class value
                      is absent from the dict are not shifted.
        :param variables: Columns to shift. Either a list of column positions (ints) or a
                          list of variable names resolvable through
                          ``selector.column_mapping``. Defaults to all columns except the
                          class column.
        :param class_column: The column holding the class values: either its position
                             (int) or a variable name resolvable through
                             ``selector.column_mapping``. The class column groups the
                             fired rows (one shift per class value) and is never shifted
                             itself. If omitted, it is recovered from the selector's
                             ``column_mapping``; when neither is available, all fired
                             rows are treated as one class and every column may be
                             shifted.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        if selector is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "FixedShiftClassesGenerator needs a selector deciding "
                "which rows shift (e.g. ClassSelector over the class "
                "column): classes are columns of X, y is not used for "
                "selection."
            )
        masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
        fired = masks[0] if len(masks) == 1 else np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
        if not fired.any():
            return X, y
        # resolve the class column: explicit parameter first, selector sniffing as fallback
        class_col = class_column
        if class_col is not None and isinstance(class_col, str):
            mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
            pos = mapping.get(class_col) if mapping is not None else None
            if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve class column {class_col!r} in X")
            class_col = pos
        elif class_col is None:
            class_col = resolve_class_column(selector, X)
        elif not (0 <= class_col < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(f"class_column {class_col} is not a valid column position in X")
        shifts = shift if isinstance(shift, dict) else None
        if shifts is not None and class_col is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "a dict shift requires a class column: pass "
                "class_column (int or name) or use a selector with "
                "column_mapping to resolve the class column position"
            )
        # resolve which columns are shifted
        if variables is not None:
            mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
            cols = []
            for var in variables:
                pos = mapping.get(var) if mapping is not None and isinstance(var, str) else var
                if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                    raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve shift column {var!r} in X")
                cols.append(pos)
            cols = np.array(sorted(set(cols)), dtype=int)
        else:
            # all columns except the class column
            cols = np.array([i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if i != class_col], dtype=int)
        if cols.size == 0:
            return X, y
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # one exact shift per class value among the fired rows
        if class_col is not None:
            values = np.unique(X[fired, class_col])
        else:
            values = np.array([None])
        for value in values:
            if shifts is not None:
                if value not in shifts:
                    continue
                shift_value = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(shifts[value], dtype=float), (cols.size,))
            elif isinstance(shift, np.ndarray) and shift.ndim == 1:
                shift_value = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(shift, dtype=float), (cols.size,))
            else:

@preprocess_inputs
def generate(self, X, y=None, *, selector=None, shift=0.1, variables=None, class_column=None):
    """
    Deterministically shift the rows fired by the selector, one exact
    shift per class value of the class column.

    :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
    :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through unchanged; not used for selection).
    :param selector: A selector deciding which rows are shifted (required; its masks
                     are OR-ed to the affected rows).
    :param shift: The exact shift applied to the fired rows of each class, in units of
                  column standard deviation (data are standardized first). A single
                  float (same shift for every class and column), a vector (one entry
                  per shifted column, same for every class), or a dict
                  ``{class_value: float or vector}`` — fired rows whose class value
                  is absent from the dict are not shifted.
    :param variables: Columns to shift. Either a list of column positions (ints) or a
                      list of variable names resolvable through
                      ``selector.column_mapping``. Defaults to all columns except the
                      class column.
    :param class_column: The column holding the class values: either its position
                         (int) or a variable name resolvable through
                         ``selector.column_mapping``. The class column groups the
                         fired rows (one shift per class value) and is never shifted
                         itself. If omitted, it is recovered from the selector's
                         ``column_mapping``; when neither is available, all fired
                         rows are treated as one class and every column may be
                         shifted.
    :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
    """
    if selector is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "FixedShiftClassesGenerator needs a selector deciding "
            "which rows shift (e.g. ClassSelector over the class "
            "column): classes are columns of X, y is not used for "
            "selection."
        )
    masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
    fired = masks[0] if len(masks) == 1 else np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
    if not fired.any():
        return X, y
    # resolve the class column: explicit parameter first, selector sniffing as fallback
    class_col = class_column
    if class_col is not None and isinstance(class_col, str):
        mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
        pos = mapping.get(class_col) if mapping is not None else None
        if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
            raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve class column {class_col!r} in X")
        class_col = pos
    elif class_col is None:
        class_col = resolve_class_column(selector, X)
    elif not (0 <= class_col < X.shape[1]):
        raise ValueError(f"class_column {class_col} is not a valid column position in X")
    shifts = shift if isinstance(shift, dict) else None
    if shifts is not None and class_col is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "a dict shift requires a class column: pass "
            "class_column (int or name) or use a selector with "
            "column_mapping to resolve the class column position"
        )
    # resolve which columns are shifted
    if variables is not None:
        mapping = getattr(selector, "column_mapping", None)
        cols = []
        for var in variables:
            pos = mapping.get(var) if mapping is not None and isinstance(var, str) else var
            if pos is None or not (0 <= pos < X.shape[1]):
                raise ValueError(f"cannot resolve shift column {var!r} in X")
            cols.append(pos)
        cols = np.array(sorted(set(cols)), dtype=int)
    else:
        # all columns except the class column
        cols = np.array([i for i in range(X.shape[1]) if i != class_col], dtype=int)
    if cols.size == 0:
        return X, y
    # normalize X
    scaler = StandardScaler()
    scaler.fit(X)
    Xt = scaler.transform(X)
    # one exact shift per class value among the fired rows
    if class_col is not None:
        values = np.unique(X[fired, class_col])
    else:
        values = np.array([None])
    for value in values:
        if shifts is not None:
            if value not in shifts:
                continue
            shift_value = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(shifts[value], dtype=float), (cols.size,))
        elif isinstance(shift, np.ndarray) and shift.ndim == 1:
            shift_value = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(shift, dtype=float), (cols.size,))
        else:
            shift_value = np.full(cols.size, float(shift))
        rows = fired if class_col is None else (fired & (X[:, class_col] == value))
        Xt[np.ix_(rows, cols)] += shift_value
    # inverse transform
    return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

class FixedShiftGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    r"""
    Deterministically shift (geometrical translation) values of each column
    independently of one another — the non-random counterpart of
    :class:`RandomShiftGenerator`.

    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1), then each column is
    translated by exactly ``shift_std``: the ith column becomes
    `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \text{shift\_std}_i$`. No random number is drawn,
    so repeated calls with the same input return the same output.
    """

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize the FixedShiftGenerator (no random generator needed)."""
        super().__init__(random_generator=None)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, shift_std: Union[float, np.array, list] = 0.1):
        r"""
        Deterministically shift each column by exactly ``shift_std``.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through unchanged; not used in this implementation).
        :param shift_std: Shift applied to each column. A single float (applied to all columns)
                          or an array of floats (one per column). The value is the shift in
                          units of column standard deviation (data are standardized first):
                          a positive entry moves the column up, a negative entry moves it
                          down. The same input always produces the same output.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        shift_std = np.asarray(shift_std, dtype=float)
        if shift_std.ndim == 1 and shift_std.size > 1:
            assert shift_std.size == X.shape[
                1], f"shift_std length ({shift_std.size}) must equal number of features in X ({X.shape[1]})"
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # exact shift per column: |shift_std| magnitude, sign(shift_std) direction
        shift = np.broadcast_to(shift_std, (X.shape[1],))
        # add shift
        Xt += shift
        # inverse transform
        return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

class RandomShiftGenerator(DriftGenerator):
    r"""
    Randomly shift (geometrical translation) values of each column independently of one another.
    Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1) and a random number is added to each column.
    The ith columns is simply translated: `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \epsilon_i$`
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        Initialize the RandomShiftGenerator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, shift_std: Union[float, np.array, list] = 0.1):
        r"""
        Randomly shift (geometrical translation) values of each column independently of one another.
        Data are first standardized (mean = 0, var = 1), and a random number drawn from a normal distribution
        with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. `shift_std` is then added to each column.
        The ith column is simply translated: `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \epsilon_i$`, where $\epsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \text{shift\_std})$.

        :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
        :param y: Target variable, a 1D array-like object (optional). Not used in this implementation.
        :param shift_std: Magnitude of the random shift applied to each column. Can be a single float
                          (applied to all columns) or an array of floats (one per column). The values
                          are interpreted as standard deviations: a random number drawn from a normal
                          distribution is multiplied by ``shift_std`` (absolute value used as the
                          scale, the sign used as the shift direction). A negative entry shifts the
                          column in the negative direction.
        :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.
        """
        # check that if shift_std is an array, it is of length == X.shape[1]
        shift_std = np.asarray(shift_std, dtype=float)
        if shift_std.ndim == 1 and shift_std.size > 1:
            assert shift_std.size == X.shape[
                1], f"shift_std length ({shift_std.size}) must equal number of features in X ({X.shape[1]})"
        # normalize X
        scaler = StandardScaler()
        scaler.fit(X)
        Xt = scaler.transform(X)
        # generate random values for the shift for each column
        # scale must be non-negative: use |shift_std| as the scale and sign(shift_std) as the direction
        scale = np.broadcast_to(np.abs(shift_std), (X.shape[1],))
        sign = np.broadcast_to(np.sign(shift_std), (X.shape[1],))
        shift = self.random_generator.normal(loc=0, scale=scale, size=X.shape[1]) * sign
        # add shift
        Xt += shift
        # inverse transform
        return scaler.inverse_transform(Xt), y

    The ith column is simply translated: `$x_i \leftarrow x_i + \epsilon_i$`, where $\epsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \text{shift\_std})$.

    :param X: Input features, a 2D array-like object (e.g., a Pandas DataFrame or a NumPy array).
    :param y: Target variable, a 1D array-like object (optional). Not used in this implementation.
    :param shift_std: Magnitude of the random shift applied to each column. Can be a single float
                      (applied to all columns) or an array of floats (one per column). The values
                      are interpreted as standard deviations: a random number drawn from a normal
                      distribution is multiplied by ``shift_std`` (absolute value used as the
                      scale, the sign used as the shift direction). A negative entry shifts the
                      column in the negative direction.
    :return: A tuple containing the modified feature matrix `X'` and the original target `y`.

            1], f"shift_std length ({shift_std.size}) must equal number of features in X ({X.shape[1]})"

class ImbalanceGenerator(GeneratorMixin):
    """
    Base class for transformers that makes tabular data imbalanced
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        Initialize the ImbalanceGenerator with a specified random number generator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        self.random_generator = random_generator
        self.imbalance_labels_: np.ndarray | None = None

    def get_imbalance_labels(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """
        Per-row imbalance labels of the LAST generated output.

        :return: A boolean array aligned with the rows of the LAST input
            passed to ``generate()``; ``True`` marks a row on which the
            deficit fired (the row was dropped from the output), ``False``
            a row that is part of the generated output.
        :raises RuntimeError: if ``generate()`` has not been called yet.
        """
        if self.imbalance_labels_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "no labels available: call generate() first "
                "(the labels describe the LAST input to generate())"
            )
        return self.imbalance_labels_

    def generate(self, X, y=None, **params):
        """
        Abstract method to generate imbalanced data from the input data.
        This should be overridden

class RandomSamplingClassesGenerator(ImbalanceGenerator):
    """
    Randomly samples data points within predefined classes
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0), ):
        """
        Initialize the RandomSamplingClassesGenerator with a specified random number generator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, selector=None):
        """
        Drops the rows fired by the selector (subsampling deficit),
        per-class: exactly ``int(prop * n_rows)`` rows of each listed class
        are removed, classes absent from the mapping are kept.

        :param X: Input features, can be a pandas DataFrame or a numpy array.
        :type X: Union[pandas.DataFrame, numpy.ndarray]
        :param y: Target variable, can be a pandas Series or a numpy array.
                  If None, it is assumed that the target is not provided.
        :type y: Union[pandas.Series, numpy.ndarray, None], optional
        :param selector: A selector (e.g.
                         :class:`badgers.core.selectors.ClassSelector`)
                         deciding which rows are dropped. ``None`` =
                         no-op (all rows kept). The class variable is a
                         column of ``X`` (resolved via the selector's
                         ``column_mapping``); ``y`` is not used for
                         selection, only passed through.
        :type selector: callable, optional
        :return: A tuple containing the sampled features (Xt) and the corresponding target values (yt).
        :rtype: Tuple[Union[pandas.DataFrame, numpy.ndarray], Union[pandas.Series, numpy.ndarray, None]]
        """
        if selector is None:
            self.imbalance_labels_ = np.zeros(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
            return X, y
        masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
        if len(masks) == 1:
            fired = masks[0]
        else:
            # a row is dropped if fired in any class column
            fired = np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
        Xt = X[~fired, :]
        yt = y[~fired] if y is not None else None
        self.imbalance_labels_ = fired
        return Xt, yt

class RandomSamplingFeaturesGenerator(ImbalanceGenerator):

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0), ):
        """
        Initialize the RandomSamplingFeaturesGenerator with a specified random number generator.
        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, sampling_proba_func=lambda X: _column_sampling_proba(X[:, 0])):
        """
        Randomly samples instances based on the feature values in X using a specified sampling probability function.

        The sampling probability function is applied to the input features X to determine the probability of each instance being sampled.
        By default, the first column of X is used to compute the normalized sampling probabilities.

        :param X: Input features, can be a pandas DataFrame or a numpy array.
        :type X: Union[pandas.DataFrame, numpy.ndarray]
        :param y: Target variable, can be a pandas Series or a numpy array.
                  If None, it is assumed that the target is not provided.
        :type y: Union[pandas.Series, numpy.ndarray, None], optional
        :param sampling_proba_func: A function that takes as input data (X) and returns a series of sampling probabilities.
                                    The function should ensure that the probabilities are normalized.
        :type sampling_proba_func: callable
        :return: A tuple containing the sampled features (Xt) and the corresponding target values (yt).
                 If y is None, only the sampled features (Xt) are returned.
        :rtype: Tuple[Union[pandas.DataFrame, numpy.ndarray], Union[pandas.Series, numpy.ndarray, None]]
        """
        # total number of instances that will be missing
        # sampling
        sampling_proba = sampling_proba_func(X)
        sampling_mask = self.random_generator.choice(X.shape[0], p=sampling_proba, size=X.shape[0], replace=True)
        Xt = X[sampling_mask, :]
        yt = y[sampling_mask] if y is not None else y
        # rows that never got drawn carry the deficit (dropped from the output)
        labels = np.ones(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
        labels[sampling_mask] = False
        self.imbalance_labels_ = labels
        return Xt, yt

Bases: ImbalanceGenerator

Resamples rows with per-row probabilities derived from a selector.

The selector decides, for each row, the probability that the deficit is applied. The deficit HERE is "this row is not kept": the generator realizes the fractional scores as KEEP weights (1 - deficit_probability, noisy-OR combined over the selector's variables) and resamples rows from those weights.

With replace=True (default) rows may be DUPLICATED -- the classic importance-resampling deficit. With replace=False the output is a weighted thinning (each row kept at most once).

class RandomSamplingTargetsGenerator(ImbalanceGenerator):
    """
    Resamples rows with per-row probabilities derived from a selector.

    The selector decides, for each row, the probability that the deficit
    is applied. The deficit HERE is "this row is not kept": the generator
    realizes the fractional scores as KEEP weights
    (``1 - deficit_probability``, noisy-OR combined over the selector's
    variables) and resamples rows from those weights.

    With ``replace=True`` (default) rows may be DUPLICATED -- the classic
    importance-resampling deficit. With ``replace=False`` the output is a
    weighted thinning (each row kept at most once).
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0)):
        """
        Initialize the RandomSamplingTargetsGenerator with a specified random number generator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, *, selector=None, replace=True, size=None):
        """
        Resamples instances from a selector's deficit probabilities.

        The selector returns per-row deficit probabilities (float scores in
        ``[0, 1]``, boolean masks being the degenerate case); rows are
        resampled with probability proportional to ``1 - p`` (i.e. rows
        with a high deficit probability are largely dropped, rows with a
        low deficit probability are kept/replicated).

        :param X: Input features, can be a pandas DataFrame or a numpy array.
        :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through; not used for selection).
        :param selector: A selector deciding which rows get the deficit.
            E.g. ``ProportionalSelector("col", column_mapping)`` (deficit
            probability proportional to a column), a ``BernoulliSelector``,
            or any callable returning ``dict[str, array]`` of per-row
            scores. Required (``None`` raises).
        :param replace: Whether to sample with replacement (default True:
            rows may be duplicated). ``False`` gives a weighted thinning.
        :param size: Number of rows to draw (default: the input row count).
        :return: A tuple (Xt, yt) of the resampled features and target.
        """
        if selector is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "RandomSamplingTargetsGenerator needs a selector deciding "
                "which rows get the deficit (e.g. ProportionalSelector "
                "over a column of X): y is not used for selection."
            )
        scores = [np.asarray(s, dtype=float) for s in selector(X, y).values()]
        if len(scores) == 1:
            deficit_proba = scores[0]
        else:
            # noisy-OR: the probabilistic generalization of the boolean OR
            keep = np.prod([1.0 - s for s in scores], axis=0)
            deficit_proba = 1.0 - keep
        if (deficit_proba < 0).any() or (deficit_proba > 1).any():
            raise ValueError(
                "selector scores must be in [0, 1] "
                f"(got [{deficit_proba.min()}, {deficit_proba.max()}])"
            )
        keep_weights = 1.0 - deficit_proba
        if not keep_weights.sum() > 0:
            raise ValueError(
                "every row has deficit probability 1: no row can be kept "
                "(lower the selector's deficit probabilities)"
            )
        # Boolean scores (all 0/1) are DETERMINISTIC: realize them as an
        # exact subsample of the rows that never fire (deficit proba 0) --
        # a weighted draw without replacement of size n would draw every
        # index once, zero-weight rows included.
        if np.isin(deficit_proba, (0.0, 1.0)).all():
            kept = np.flatnonzero(deficit_proba == 0.0)
            if size is not None and size < len(kept):
                kept = self.random_generator.choice(kept, size=size, replace=False)
            Xt = X[kept, :]
            yt = y[kept] if y is not None else None
            fired = np.ones(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
            fired[kept] = False
            self.imbalance_labels_ = fired
            return Xt, yt
        # Fractional scores: normalize the keep weights into a probability
        # vector and resample from them.
        p = normalize_proba(keep_weights.reshape(-1, 1)).ravel()
        n = self.random_generator.choice(
            X.shape[0], p=p, size=X.shape[0] if size is None else size,
            replace=replace,
        )
        Xt = X[n, :]
        yt = y[n] if y is not None else None
        fired = np.ones(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
        fired[n] = False
        self.imbalance_labels_ = fired
        return Xt, yt

@preprocess_inputs
def generate(self, X, y=None, *, selector=None, replace=True, size=None):
    """
    Resamples instances from a selector's deficit probabilities.

    The selector returns per-row deficit probabilities (float scores in
    ``[0, 1]``, boolean masks being the degenerate case); rows are
    resampled with probability proportional to ``1 - p`` (i.e. rows
    with a high deficit probability are largely dropped, rows with a
    low deficit probability are kept/replicated).

    :param X: Input features, can be a pandas DataFrame or a numpy array.
    :param y: Target variable (optional, passed through; not used for selection).
    :param selector: A selector deciding which rows get the deficit.
        E.g. ``ProportionalSelector("col", column_mapping)`` (deficit
        probability proportional to a column), a ``BernoulliSelector``,
        or any callable returning ``dict[str, array]`` of per-row
        scores. Required (``None`` raises).
    :param replace: Whether to sample with replacement (default True:
        rows may be duplicated). ``False`` gives a weighted thinning.
    :param size: Number of rows to draw (default: the input row count).
    :return: A tuple (Xt, yt) of the resampled features and target.
    """
    if selector is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "RandomSamplingTargetsGenerator needs a selector deciding "
            "which rows get the deficit (e.g. ProportionalSelector "
            "over a column of X): y is not used for selection."
        )
    scores = [np.asarray(s, dtype=float) for s in selector(X, y).values()]
    if len(scores) == 1:
        deficit_proba = scores[0]
    else:
        # noisy-OR: the probabilistic generalization of the boolean OR
        keep = np.prod([1.0 - s for s in scores], axis=0)
        deficit_proba = 1.0 - keep
    if (deficit_proba < 0).any() or (deficit_proba > 1).any():
        raise ValueError(
            "selector scores must be in [0, 1] "
            f"(got [{deficit_proba.min()}, {deficit_proba.max()}])"
        )
    keep_weights = 1.0 - deficit_proba
    if not keep_weights.sum() > 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "every row has deficit probability 1: no row can be kept "
            "(lower the selector's deficit probabilities)"
        )
    # Boolean scores (all 0/1) are DETERMINISTIC: realize them as an
    # exact subsample of the rows that never fire (deficit proba 0) --
    # a weighted draw without replacement of size n would draw every
    # index once, zero-weight rows included.
    if np.isin(deficit_proba, (0.0, 1.0)).all():
        kept = np.flatnonzero(deficit_proba == 0.0)
        if size is not None and size < len(kept):
            kept = self.random_generator.choice(kept, size=size, replace=False)
        Xt = X[kept, :]
        yt = y[kept] if y is not None else None
        fired = np.ones(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
        fired[kept] = False
        self.imbalance_labels_ = fired
        return Xt, yt
    # Fractional scores: normalize the keep weights into a probability
    # vector and resample from them.
    p = normalize_proba(keep_weights.reshape(-1, 1)).ravel()
    n = self.random_generator.choice(
        X.shape[0], p=p, size=X.shape[0] if size is None else size,
        replace=replace,
    )
    Xt = X[n, :]
    yt = y[n] if y is not None else None
    fired = np.ones(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
    fired[n] = False
    self.imbalance_labels_ = fired
    return Xt, yt

class CausalImbalanceGenerator(CausalGenerator):
    """Generates selection bias as a quantile-range truncation (imbalance).

    The row selection is observation-side only: rows whose perturbation-node
    values fall outside ``quantile_range`` are removed; kept rows are
    returned untouched (a pure subset). No DGP is required.

    Parameters
    ----------
    random_generator : numpy.random.Generator, default=rng(seed=0)
        Random number generator instance.

    generate() parameters (passed via **params)
    ----------
    selector : Selector or None, default=None
        Row-selection rule from ``badgers.core.selectors``. The rows FIRED
        by the selector are dropped (subsampling polarity: ``True`` =
        deficit applied = row removed); with multiple variables the union
        of fired rows is dropped. ``None`` falls back to the
        ``perturbation_nodes`` + ``quantile_range`` rule below.
    perturbation_nodes : list of str
        Nodes whose quantile ranges define the kept set (only used when
        ``selector=None``).
    quantile_range : tuple of (float, float), default=(0.5, 1.0)
        Quantile range of the perturbation node's values that is KEPT. With
        multiple perturbation nodes, the kept set is the intersection of all
        ranges. Rows outside are removed (in-place subset). Only used when
        ``selector=None``.
    """

    deficit_name = "imbalance"

    def get_imbalance_labels(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return the imbalance labels of the last generated output.

        A boolean vector aligned with the rows of the last generated
        output: True for rows that carry the imbalance deficit (the kept
        subset), False for... none (all kept rows are affected).
        """
        if self.deficit_labels_ is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Imbalance labels are only available after calling "
                "generate()."
            )
        return self.deficit_labels_

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(
        self,
        X,
        y,
        selector=None,
        perturbation_nodes=None,
        quantile_range=(0.5, 1.0),
    ):
        """Inject causally-propagated imbalance in place (subset of rows)."""
        self._require_fitted()
        n_samples = X.shape[0]

        if selector is not None:
            # Explicit selector: rows FIRED by the selector are dropped
            # (subsampling polarity). Union over the selector's variables.
            dropped = np.zeros(n_samples, dtype=bool)
            for mask in selector(X, y).values():
                dropped |= np.asarray(mask, dtype=bool)
            keep = ~dropped
        else:
            self._validate_structure(X)
            self._validate_perturbation_nodes(perturbation_nodes)
            node_to_col = self.column_mapping
            # Legacy quantile-range rule: keep rows inside the intersection
            # of all perturbation-node ranges.
            lo, hi = quantile_range
            if not (0.0 <= lo < hi <= 1.0):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"quantile_range must satisfy 0 <= lo < hi <= 1, "
                    f"got {quantile_range}"
                )
            keep = np.ones(n_samples, dtype=bool)
            for node in perturbation_nodes:
                col = node_to_col[node]
                b_lo = np.quantile(X[:, col], lo)
                b_hi = np.quantile(X[:, col], hi)
                keep &= (X[:, col] >= b_lo) & (X[:, col] <= b_hi)

        X = X[keep]
        if y is not None:
            y = y[keep]
        affected = np.ones(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)

        self.deficit_labels_ = affected.copy()
        return X, None

class RandomSamplingClassesGenerator(ImbalanceGenerator):
    """
    Randomly samples data points within predefined classes
    """

    def __init__(self, random_generator=default_rng(seed=0), ):
        """
        Initialize the RandomSamplingClassesGenerator with a specified random number generator.

        :param random_generator: A NumPy random number generator used to generate random numbers.
                                 Defaults to a default random number generator seeded with 0.
        :type random_generator: numpy.random.Generator
        """
        super().__init__(random_generator=random_generator)

    @preprocess_inputs
    def generate(self, X, y=None, selector=None):
        """
        Drops the rows fired by the selector (subsampling deficit),
        per-class: exactly ``int(prop * n_rows)`` rows of each listed class
        are removed, classes absent from the mapping are kept.

        :param X: Input features, can be a pandas DataFrame or a numpy array.
        :type X: Union[pandas.DataFrame, numpy.ndarray]
        :param y: Target variable, can be a pandas Series or a numpy array.
                  If None, it is assumed that the target is not provided.
        :type y: Union[pandas.Series, numpy.ndarray, None], optional
        :param selector: A selector (e.g.
                         :class:`badgers.core.selectors.ClassSelector`)
                         deciding which rows are dropped. ``None`` =
                         no-op (all rows kept). The class variable is a
                         column of ``X`` (resolved via the selector's
                         ``column_mapping``); ``y`` is not used for
                         selection, only passed through.
        :type selector: callable, optional
        :return: A tuple containing the sampled features (Xt) and the corresponding target values (yt).
        :rtype: Tuple[Union[pandas.DataFrame, numpy.ndarray], Union[pandas.Series, numpy.ndarray, None]]
        """
        if selector is None:
            self.imbalance_labels_ = np.zeros(X.shape[0], dtype=bool)
            return X, y
        masks = list(selector(X, y).values())
        if len(masks) == 1:
            fired = masks[0]
        else:
            # a row is dropped if fired in any class column
            fired = np.logical_or.reduce(masks)
        Xt = X[~fired, :]
        yt = y[~fired] if y is not None else None
        self.imbalance_labels_ = fired
        return Xt, yt

Bases: ImbalanceGenerator

Resamples rows with per-row probabilities derived from a selector.

The selector decides, for each row, the probability that the deficit is applied. The deficit HERE is "this row is not kept": the generator realizes the fractional scores as KEEP weights (1 - deficit_probability, noisy-OR combined over the selector's variables) and resamples rows from those weights.

With replace=True (default) rows may be DUPLICATED -- the classic importance-resampling deficit. With replace=False the output is a weighted thinning (each row kept at most once).
